title: Cosmic Microwave Background and Nucleosynthesis
welcome_lead: Two pillars of Big Bang evidence — and where the elements came.
meta_desc: A-Level Astronomy: CMB, recombination and Big Bang nucleosynthesis.
final_note: Two predictions of Big Bang theory confirmed by observation.

concepts.def: Cosmic Microwave Background — relic radiation from the early universe.
When electrons combined with nuclei, freeing photons.
Production of the lightest elements in the first minutes.
Moment photons stopped scattering off free electrons.
Surface from which CMB photons last interacted with matter.
A body emitting thermal radiation depending only on temperature.

walkthroughs.body_html: The CMB, discovered by Penzias and Wilson in 1964, is a near-perfect blackbody at about 2.7 K. Tiny anisotropies seed today's structures and reveal the universe's geometry.
About 380,000 years after the Big Bang, the universe cooled to 3000 K and electrons combined with nuclei. The universe became transparent — this is the surface of last scattering.
In the first minutes, Big Bang nucleosynthesis produced about 75% hydrogen, 25% helium-4 by mass, plus traces of deuterium and lithium. Heavier elements were forged later in stars.
